name: Trengo
tagline: The Dutch omnichannel inbox that ran three years on zero outside capital before raising $39.9M — now automating what it calls 'the boring 84%' of repetitive support questions.
tldr: Trengo was founded in 2017 in Utrecht, the Netherlands by Patrick Meutzner, Marcel van de Weerd, and Igo Trampe, bootstrapped to roughly 15 people before raising €1.75M in 2020 and a $36M Series A in 2021 led by Insight Partners and Peak Capital — $39.9M total, now serving 3,000+ customers globally.

Pricing is per-workspace with included user counts: Boost at €299/mo annual (€349 month-to-month) for 10 users, Pro at €499/mo annual (€599 month-to-month) for 20 users, and custom Enterprise — a conversation-allowance model rather than pure per-seat billing.

The AI positioning is distinctive: rather than claiming to handle everything, Trengo frames its AI Agents around automating 'the boring 84%' — the repetitive questions nobody wants to answer twice — with chatbots and agent-assist tools drawing from a connected knowledge base.

Genuinely deep native CRM integrations stand out: connecting Salesforce or HubSpot surfaces contact records, lead status, and sales data directly inside the Trengo inbox without switching tabs, alongside native Shopify, Magento, and WooCommerce integrations.
Analytics are comprehensive and specific — first response time, resolution rate, ticket deflection rate, CSAT, bot containment rate, and escalation frequency are all documented as tracked metrics.

The most serious, recurring independent-review complaint isn't a missing feature — it's pricing instability: multiple reviewers specifically describe prices doubling with sudden changes and critical features being phased out, a real trust concern worth weighing against the otherwise strong product.
keyFeatures: AI Agents positioned around automating repetitive, high-volume questions ('the boring 84%') rather than claiming universal resolution capability
Customizable, no-code chatbots and agent-assist tools that draw from a connected knowledge base for instant, relevant answers
Smart ticket routing and workflow automation across all connected channels
Deep native Salesforce and HubSpot integrations surfacing contact records, lead status, and sales data directly inside the Trengo inbox
Native Shopify, Magento, and WooCommerce integrations for ecommerce-context conversations
Quick replies (canned responses), internal notes, and @mentions for team coordination without exposing internal discussion to customers
Comprehensive analytics tracking first response time, resolution rate, ticket deflection rate, CSAT, bot containment rate, and escalation frequency
Shared dashboards and workload-balancing tools for distributing conversation volume across a team

faq.question: What does Trengo mean by automating 'the boring 84%'?
faq.answer: It's the company's own framing for its AI positioning: rather than marketing its AI as capable of resolving everything, Trengo specifically targets the repetitive, low-complexity questions that make up the bulk of support volume but that agents don't want to keep answering by hand — leaving more complex or judgment-heavy conversations for humans. It's a more modest, arguably more honest framing than some competitors' universal-resolution marketing.

faq.question: How much does Trengo actually cost?
faq.answer: Boost is €299/month billed annually (€349 month-to-month) for 10 users, and Pro is €499/month annually (€599 month-to-month) for 20 users, with custom Enterprise pricing above that. It's a per-workspace, conversation-allowance model rather than strict per-seat billing, so review the specific conversation cap on your tier rather than assuming unlimited volume.

faq.question: What is the most serious complaint about Trengo?
faq.answer: Pricing stability, and it's specific rather than vague. Multiple independent reviewers describe prices doubling with what they characterize as sudden changes, and separately report critical features being phased out after a price increase. This is a different, more serious kind of concern than a typical 'it's expensive' complaint — it's about trust in the pricing relationship over time, and worth asking about directly before signing an annual contract.

faq.question: How deep is Trengo's CRM integration?
faq.answer: Genuinely deep for both major CRMs it supports: connecting Salesforce or HubSpot pulls contact records, lead status, company details, and sales data directly into the Trengo inbox, so agents don't need to switch tabs to get context. This is a real strength relative to competitors whose CRM integrations only sync basic contact fields.

faq.question: Does Trengo work well for ecommerce support?
faq.answer: There's real, native integration support for Shopify, Magento, and WooCommerce, which is broader ecommerce-platform coverage than several competitors offer. We didn't find the same level of documented detail on order-editing or refund actions that ecommerce-first specialists like Gorgias or Re:amaze publish, so test the specific depth you need directly.

faq.question: What is Trengo's real AI resolution rate?
faq.answer: Some third-party sources cite figures around 80% resolution, but no independently audited benchmark was found to verify this. As with any vendor-adjacent AI performance claim in this category, treat it as an upper-bound estimate under favorable conditions rather than a typical guaranteed outcome.

pricingBreakdown: Trengo's published pricing (€299/mo Boost, €499/mo Pro) is reasonably competitive for a 10-to-20-user team against comparable per-seat competitors, and the conversation-allowance model rather than strict per-seat billing can favor teams with more users but moderate individual conversation volume. What's genuinely concerning, and worth weighing more heavily than the sticker price itself, is the pattern independent reviewers describe: prices reportedly doubling with sudden changes, and critical features being phased out after an increase. That's a materially different risk than a competitor simply being expensive — it's a signal that the pricing relationship itself may not be stable over a multi-year commitment. Before signing an annual contract, ask directly about historical pricing changes and get any promised feature continuity in writing rather than assuming the current published tier structure will hold.

capabilities.note: This is Trengo's founding thesis and its clearest strength: WhatsApp, Facebook, SMS, web chat, Telegram, email, and voice all land in one inbox, and independent reviewers consistently confirm this works well in daily use, with several specifically praising the pace of new channel additions.

A genuinely more credible AI framing than many competitors': rather than claiming to resolve everything, Trengo explicitly targets the repetitive, high-volume questions that eat up agent time, leaving more nuanced conversations for humans. It's a modest claim, which also makes it a more trustworthy one — though still without independent verification of the underlying resolution rate.

Genuinely deep native Salesforce and HubSpot integrations pull contact and sales data directly into the inbox, a real strength versus competitors offering only shallow contact sync. Shopify, Magento, and WooCommerce integrations extend this to ecommerce, though with less documented depth on order-specific actions.

One of the more comprehensive, specifically-named analytics suites found in this category — first response time, resolution rate, deflection rate, CSAT, bot containment rate, and escalation frequency are all documented as tracked metrics, giving a genuinely fuller picture than a basic volume-and-response-time dashboard.

The one area where I'd urge real caution independent of the product's actual capability. A specific, repeated reviewer complaint pattern — prices doubling, features phased out after increases — is a trust signal worth investigating directly with the vendor before committing to any multi-year plan, regardless of how competitive the currently published price looks.

verdict: Trengo built something genuinely solid on its own terms before ever taking outside money — three years bootstrapped to fifteen people, then real institutional backing ($39.9M from Insight Partners and Peak Capital) to scale a product whose core idea, one inbox for every channel, still holds up well according to independent reviewers. The CRM integrations are a real, specific strength: connecting Salesforce or HubSpot pulls contact and sales data directly into the inbox rather than a shallow contact-sync, and the analytics suite is genuinely more detailed than most competitors', tracking bot containment rate and escalation frequency alongside the standard response-time metrics. The AI framing — automating 'the boring 84%' rather than claiming to resolve everything — is a more modest, more credible position than some competitors' universal-resolution marketing, even though there's no independent audit to verify the underlying accuracy either way. What genuinely gives me pause, and what I'd weigh more heavily than the sticker price itself, is a specific and repeated complaint pattern in independent reviews: prices reportedly doubling with sudden changes, and critical features being phased out after an increase. That's not the usual 'it's a bit pricey' grumble — it's a signal about whether the pricing relationship holds steady over time, and it's serious enough that I'd want it addressed directly, in writing, before committing to an annual contract. My honest read: the product itself is genuinely strong, particularly on CRM depth and analytics, and the AI positioning is refreshingly honest about its scope. But go into any Trengo negotiation with the pricing-stability question already on the table, not as an afterthought once you're locked in.
